cohort: The study included 143 women/infant pairs, comprising 62 infants born via elective caesarean section and 81 via emergency caesarean section.
finding: Early-term surgical delivery (elective caesarean section) is identified as a determinant of transient dilutional anaemia in neonates, linked to a lack of neuroendocrine response of labour and delivery.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered by elective caesarean section exhibited significantly lower cord blood haematocrit levels at birth, greater body weight decrease, and a higher subsequent haematocrit increase at 48 hours compared to those delivered by emergency caesarean section.
